newsitem.title: USA: Spiegel cites lower catalog productivity.
newsitem.headline: Spiegel cites lower catalog productivity.

text.p: Spiegel Inc, reporting lower fourth-quarter results and a larger loss for the full year, said its Spiegel Catalog and Newport News businesses were hurt by tightened credit policies and lower productivity from catalog mailings.
"In addition, the continued industrywide trend toward higher charge-offs, particularly bankruptcies, affected our credit performance," said vice chairman and president John Shea in a statement.

The company's technology consulting subsidiary in the first quarter of 1996 also contributed to the revenue decline. In addition, Spiegel said it reported a gain of $18.6 million from the sale of receivables in 1995, with no comparable gains reported in 1996.
Shea said Spiegel's Eddie Bauer business achieved record results, with comparable-store sales for the subsidiary rising one percent for the 13 weeks ended December 28.
The Spiegel Group's catalog businesses, including Spiegel, Eddie Bauer and Newport News, generated net sales of $1.67 billion in 1996 compared with $1.75 billion in 1995.

Shea said, "Spiegel Catalog's restructured management team has developed and is implementing new strategies to regain market share. These strategies will evolve in 1997 and are directed at reestablishing Spiegel Catalog as the fashion and style authority for today's busy woman."
Shea added that the company plans to open up to 70 stores in North America this year, expanding internationally through Eddie Bauer's joint venture agreements.

Earlier, Spiegel reported earnings of $0.18 a share compared with $0.35 the prior year for the fourth quarter and a loss of $0.12 a share for the full year compared to a year-ago loss of $0.09 a share.
